report.summary: Chunk 9 of 11: implements _run_rewrite and _rewrite_by_window logic for windowed and full-file edits, with error handling and skip reasons.
risks: _rewrite_by_window | medium | The function uses a fixed retry count of 2 attempts per window; if the model consistently fails, the whole file edit may be aborted without fallback. | Check if retry count is configurable or if fallback to full-file rewrite exists.

_run_rewrite | medium | The function limits to MAX_REWRITE_FILES files; if paths exceed this, remaining files are silently ignored. | Verify that MAX_REWRITE_FILES is documented and that callers handle truncation.

_run_rewrite | medium | The windowed path preserves original line endings (raw) while the full-rewrite path normalizes to LF. This inconsistency could cause byte-level differences. | Confirm that the caller expects this behavior or that both paths are aligned.
todos: Check if _rewrite_by_window is defined elsewhere in the file.
Verify that MAX_REWRITE_FILES constant exists and is set appropriately.
Ensure that the windowed and full-rewrite paths have consistent line-ending handling.

handoff.purpose: Implement _run_rewrite and _rewrite_by_window for file editing with windowed and full-file strategies.

claims.text: The live benchmark showed 7B-class models narrate edits but never emit write_file calls -- yet the same model reliably returns the COMPLETE edited file as json.
claims.why: No benchmark data or model behavior is present in this chunk.

claims.text: So: model returns content, the harness writes it deterministically, the verifier still gates it.
claims.why: This chunk shows _run_rewrite receiving content from model and writing to files (via out list).

claims.text: Every skip reason is recorded so a no-op escalation is explainable instead of silent.
claims.why: The function maintains 'skipped' dict and 'dropped' list to record reasons.

claims.text: Greenfield CREATE: a path that doesn't exist yet is a creation request, not an error -- the same guard gates it, the backup is None (rollback deletes it), and the quality checks that compare against the original are skipped because there is no original.
claims.why: Backup and rollback logic are not present in this chunk; only the 'creating' flag is set.

claims.text: WINDOWED path: the caller named the lines that are wrong, so the model is asked for those lines instead of a reprint. No hint (or an unusable one) falls through to the unchanged full-file behaviour below -- a window is never invented here.
claims.why: The code checks 'if windows:' and only calls _rewrite_by_window when windows exist; otherwise falls to full-file path.

claims.text: Keep raw decoded line endings for byte-stable splicing.
claims.why: In the windowed branch, 'original = disk_original' preserves raw line endings.

claims.text: Preserve the pre-window full-rewrite contract: text-mode reads expose universal newlines to the prompt and text-mode writes restore the platform convention.
claims.why:
In the else branch, 'original = disk_original.replace("
", "
").replace("", "
")' normalizes to universal newlines.

observations.what: The _rewrite_by_window function uses a hardcoded timeout of min(float(timeout_s), 60.0) and retries up to 2 times per window.
The _run_rewrite function limits the number of files to MAX_REWRITE_FILES and silently ignores the rest.
The windowed branch uses raw line endings (original = disk_original) while the full-rewrite branch normalizes to LF.
